data: Klimax is a decentralized perpetual futures exchange (Perpetual DEX) on the Klaytn network that introduced an oracle-based architecture to overcome the limitations of the existing futureDEX. I participated in frontend and smart contract development and planning.
data.background#Background:
Existing DEXs on the Klaytn network focused on spot trading, making it difficult to profit in declining or low-volatility markets. futureDEX supported long/short and leveraged trading but had the following issues:
Futures-Spot Price Gap (Price Pegging): Potential for unintended losses due to price discrepancies between exchanges
Price Impact: Price slippage during trade execution due to insufficient liquidity
Lack of CEX-Level UX: Slow execution speeds, repetitive wallet approvals, and other user experience limitations
data.oracle-based-architecture#Oracle-Based A:
Referencing GMX's architecture as a representative oracle-based exchange, Klimax addressed these issues as follows:
Price Pegging: Trades are executed based on spot prices from centralized exchanges like Binance, reducing the futures-spot price gap to near zero
Zero Price Impact: Utilizes its own liquidity pool to eliminate price slippage during trades
Streamlined UI/UX: Kept only essential features, providing a user experience optimized for the blockchain environment
data.key-differentiators#Key Differentiators:
Solving the Oracle Gap: Developed a proprietary price feed system to address the lack of reliable oracles on the Klaytn network
Fee Reduction: Minimized trading fees by eliminating unnecessary procedures
Optimized Liquidity Pool: Stablecoin-centric liquidity pool that minimizes liquidity provider loss risk and enables efficient operations

data:
A service that shows monthly visitor trends for over 200 domestic trade areas and 500+ consumer brand stores.
Started as a small promotional project for Loplat and Loplat i. After learning SSR and D3.js, I completed the release within the deadline.Averaging 1,000 monthly visitors, the service is primarily used by press outlets.Visit
data.internal-review#Internal Review:
Received positive feedback: "What started as a prototype turned into a bigger project than expected. Despite delayed planning, the release was completed on schedule."
Pair programming was adopted right before deployment: "By quickly exchanging knowledge in a short time, we were able to deploy reliably."
data.tech-stack#Tech Stack: NextJS, D3.js, Recoil, Typescript, ESLint, Prettier, Tailwind, styled-components, Firestore, Google Analytics, storybook, Vercel
data.project-setup#Project Setup:
Used NextJS + SSG for SEO and fast rendering.
At build time, statically generated 600+ brand and trade area pages, while chart data is fetched on the client side.
Used Presentational and Container Component Pattern instead of Atomic Design.
Specifically, structured code into container (business logic) and foundation (UI based on props).
Decided against Atomic Design due to unclear boundaries between atom and molecule, which can cause confusion. The cost of reaching consensus on boundaries is itself a cost, and even with consensus, it's not meaningfully productive. Reference
Introduced Recoil to persist the user's previously selected brand/trade area tab.
A known issue: Recoil generated console warnings in SSR environments regardless of whether it was functioning — a point for future refactoring.
data.pc--mobile-responsive#PC / Mobile Respon:
Considering SSR characteristics, used CSS media queries instead of client-side window.width detection for UI branching.
Used Tailwind to improve CSS and media query readability.
data.trending-brandstrade-areas-ranking#Trend: Developed a list of brands/trade areas with significant changes in visitor trends over the past 7 days.
data.search-autocomplete#Search Autocomplete: Calculated similarity scores for each brand/trade area's official name, Korean name, and English name, then populated the autocomplete list with the highest-scoring items.
data.custom-hook#Custom Hook:
Extracted the search-results-by-input logic into useList to prevent code duplication.
Users can receive text alerts about visitor changes for a specific brand/trade area. Extracted the logic for updating or adding non-duplicate alerts (given brand/trade area name and phone number) into useAlarm.

data:
An internal back office for classifying and reviewing collected WiFi signals and store information, and managing inquiries and requests from users of the location data collection app.This was the first project I worked on after joining.
The existing Vue-based back office had issues including uncontrolled two-way bindings, high inter-component coupling, mixed style code and business logic, and insufficient documentation with no traceable history. I migrated it to React.
I also proposed the first adoption of TypeScript to improve developer experience.
data.internal-review#Internal Review:
Received positive feedback: "Features were well implemented despite the lack of documented company history, and documentation was thorough."
"Did their best in a situation where there was no dedicated planner or manager."
"Went from learning TypeScript to actual adoption in a short time, achieving significant improvements."

data.presentational-and-container-component-p:
Used Presentational and Container Component Pattern instead of Atomic Design.
Specifically, structured code into container (business logic) and foundation (UI based on props).
Decided against Atomic Design due to unclear boundaries between atom and molecule, which can cause confusion. The cost of reaching consensus on boundaries is itself a cost, and even with consensus, it's not meaningfully productive. Reference
Built reusable components that are not dependent on parent components.
The original table component handled data formatting internally with conditional logic for each page's different data formats.
Refactored so that the parent passes the necessary format functions, rather than having the child component specify data formatting.
Experienced improved maintainability and readability when breaking large logic into small pure functions.
data.typescript-adoption#TypeScript Adoption:
Proposed and adopted TypeScript for the first time to ensure API consistency. Also conducted a seminar to improve colleagues' TypeScript understanding and usage.
Achieved improved developer experience by maintaining consistent and stable data types from API responses to UI rendering.

data:
Nego is a service where users search for products and add them to a wishlist. Even if different product listings are selected, the algorithm extracts product IDs and consolidates identical products for unified management.
A crawling engine then runs on a set schedule, stores pricing data, and displays price trend graphs. Users receive notifications when their desired price or price fluctuation is detected.
data.work#Work: I maintained the existing iOS app written in Swift2, and developed the price change graph, do-not-disturb mode, and wishlist features using Realm and Storyboard.

/posts/career/wb-newsletter.title: Internal Newsletter That Made a Difference

data:
I curated articles previously shared by team members, company news that internal staff were often unaware of, and work-related content providing insights and food for thought — delivered weekly via Slack. I personally selected and shared columns on various topics including communication, development, and writing.At the time, many new members had recently joined, and with new service planning being delayed, there were frequent requests for updates on the company's internal situation.
Simply sharing company news alone would have felt like a noisy KakaoTalk announcement channel — creating a stiff atmosphere and failing to elicit feedback from employees.
So I decided to combine articles shared across team Slack channels, columns I had personally read, and even music recommendations from team members — delivering it all like a radio show format.
data.details#Details:
Considering the team was 10 people (all male), the thread replies and emoji reactions on Slack were remarkable.
The company recognized the newsletter as a significant contribution to fostering a horizontal organizational culture.
